title: marionette
subtitle: Gesture-controlled Spotify player
overview: Controlling Spotify with nothing but your hands in front of a webcam — reliably, regardless of how far away or where in the frame the hand sits.
body: Controlling music playback with nothing but your hands in front of a webcam — no keyboard, no phone, no wearable. The hard part isn't reading a hand once; it's reading it reliably no matter how far it is from the camera or where it sits in the frame.

It started as GestureForge, a v1 with hard-coded, rule-based gesture logic — if the fingers look roughly like this, do that. It worked, but it was brittle, and it didn't really teach me anything about the actual problem. Marionette is the rewrite: a webcam feed goes through MediaPipe for hand landmark detection, then through a custom normalised feature vector I designed so a gesture looks the same to the model whether the hand is near or far, left or right. A KNN classifier takes that vector and predicts the gesture, which maps to a Spotify action — play, pause, skip.

The feature normalisation is the part I'm actually proud of — it wasn't borrowed from anywhere, and it's what makes recognition position- and scale-invariant. Going from GestureForge's hard-coded rules to Marionette's trained KNN classifier is a clean example of moving from heuristics to something actually data-driven.
Built and shipped, and documented publicly in a couple of LinkedIn write-ups.
